Efficient Grass With PCG - Procedural Content Generation (PCG) - Episode 2
recent_posts.summary: A step-by-step walkthrough of building a runtime GPU-based grass spawning system in Unreal Engine using PCG (Procedural Content Generation). Covers the difference between static CPU-based and runtime GPU-based point generation, setting up grid tiles and partitioning, controlling tile size and spawn distances, configuring cull distances with start/end fade zones, disabling expensive rendering features like shadows and indirect lighting for performance, and setting up the material's per-instance fade amount node to enable smooth grass fade-out at distance.

recent_posts.title: Introduction to Procedural Content Generation (PCG) - Episode 1
recent_posts.summary: An introductory episode in a series on Procedural Content Generation (PCG) in Unreal Engine. Covers what PCG is, why it's superior to manual environment placement, and walks through a basic hands-on example: enabling the PCG plugin, creating a PCG graph, generating a point grid, spawning static mesh ferns, and applying random transforms for organic placement. PCG became production-ready in Unreal Engine 5.7, enabling dynamic, rule-based environments that update automatically when rules change.

recent_posts.title: Landscape Puddles - Terrain Shaders - Episode 19
recent_posts.summary: A tutorial on adding dynamic puddles to Unreal Engine landscape terrain shaders. Covers creating a weather puddles landscape material function, setting up a puddle mask to control placement (flat areas only), configuring material instance parameters for puddle accumulation, color, and opacity, and adding animated ripple effects for both wind and rain using a separate weather puddle ripples material function. The tutorial references four prior episodes (16, 17, 29, 30) for building prerequisite material functions, and explains how to split static and animated effects for compatibility with virtual textures.

recent_posts.title: Rain Effects On Terrain - Terrain Shaders - Episode 18
recent_posts.summary: A step-by-step walkthrough for adding rain effects to terrain in Unity using Shader Graph. Covers importing the production-ready shaders sample from the Unity Package Manager, adapting the built-in rain floor subgraph to work with a custom 4x4 matrix-based terrain material system, creating a custom puddles terrain subgraph, wiring up is-raining and puddle-size parameters, and using height data to break up puddle edge shapes for more realistic results.

recent_posts.title: Overridable Auto Material - Terrain Shaders - Episode 17
recent_posts.summary: A tutorial covering how to add manual paint override capability to an auto terrain material in both Unreal Engine and Unity. The auto material automatically applies grass, dirt, rocks, and snow based on slope angle and altitude, but artists often need to manually override specific areas. In Unreal, this involves setting up target layers with layer info objects and inserting a Landscape Layer Blend node into the material graph. In Unity, the equivalent is achieved using a height-based splat modify node combined with custom layer blending logic. Both approaches allow the auto material to remain the default while enabling painters to override specific terrain patches with chosen materials.

recent_posts.title: Terrain Advanced Auto Material - Terrain Shaders - Episode 16
recent_posts.summary: Episode 16 of a terrain shader series demonstrates building an advanced auto material for terrain in both Unreal Engine and Unity. The material automatically blends grass, cliff, dirt, and snow layers based on terrain slope and altitude using three key tools: an altitude mask (black-to-white gradient between two world-space heights), a terrain angle mask (gradient based on slope angle with pixel normal support for detail), and a height lerp node (blends layers using each material's height data). In Unreal, the workflow covers blending mossy and rocky grass via height lerp driven by altitude, blending dirt and cliff materials by altitude on slopes, combining slope and grass groups via terrain angle mask, and adding altitude+angle-driven snow that creeps down steeper angles at higher elevations. The Unity section mirrors this approach using equivalent shader nodes, including tile-break layers to reduce tiling artifacts and a lerp-driven mask center for realistic snow distribution.

recent_posts.title: Terrain Altitude Blending - Terrain Shaders - Episode 15
recent_posts.summary: This tutorial demonstrates how to blend terrain materials based on altitude in both Unity and Unreal Engine. The technique uses an altitude mask to transition between lowland grass and highland rocky grass materials. Instead of a simple linear blend, the altitude mask drives a terrain angle mask's center value, creating more realistic transitions by combining altitude-based blending with slope angle calculations. The method involves creating custom shader nodes, using world position data to calculate height gradients, and remapping values through linear interpolation to control cone angle masks that respect surface normals.
